minutes.headline: Board delayed two large subdivisions over storm-water/wildlife concerns; approved several smaller projects
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board approved several smaller land-use requests (a duplex conversion on Reservoir Road, a driveway/storm water modification on Arbor Street, and a storm water permit on Mass Ave), while continuing two larger multi-lot subdivisions (Parmenter/Round Road and 860 New Westminster Road) to July 27 pending engineering follow-up, an HOA/maintenance mechanism, and a fire-system cistern review. Residents raised concerns about runoff, driveway placement, and a possible wildlife corridor on Parmenter Road, and the board separately discussed reworking its inclusionary housing and common-driveway bylaws over the summer.

what_happened.line: The board continued two multi-lot subdivisions, Parmenter/Round Road and 860 New Westminster Road, to July 27 for more engineering and maintenance review.
Residents raised concerns about storm-water runoff toward Lake Shirley, driveway placement, and a possible wildlife corridor on Parmenter Road.
The board approved three smaller items: a duplex conversion on Reservoir Road, a driveway and storm-water change on Arbor Street, and a storm-water permit on Mass Ave.
A vote on the draft master plan update was pushed back two weeks so members can finish reviewing it individually.

why_it_matters: Homeowners near Parmenter/Round Road and New Westminster Road will see construction timing hinge on a maintenance mechanism (HOA or covenant) and a fire-system cistern review still being worked out.
Runoff and possible wildlife-corridor questions raised by neighbors could affect lot layout and tree clearing before those subdivisions get final approval.
The board is also weighing changes to its common-driveway and inclusionary-housing bylaws over the summer, which could affect how future subdivisions and duplex conversions are permitted.
